- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.68) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 85–87 and adjust downward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) in last 3–5 days, model overconfidently holds high forecasts; reduce forecast by 3–6% for next 5–7 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >85 for 3+ consecutive days, true price tends to drop 5–10% in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 2–5% to align with true trend.
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative cycles, model tends to lag in adjusting to sentiment shifts; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days if sentiment flips.
